A support engineer is reviewing a service incident. The deployment remained healthy, but one availability zone showed elevated request latency for several minutes. The engineer checks the request trace, cache statistics, and deployment timeline before writing a concise assessment.

Task:
input.source_suffix_text: Summarize the most likely operational cause and propose two diagnostic checks.
input.modified_suffix_text: Explain which measurements would distinguish a cache-capacity event from network congestion.

input.prefix_text:
An analyst is comparing two language-model serving configurations under the same workload. Both configurations receive identical prompts and use greedy decoding. One configuration recomputes every prefix, while the other reuses a token-identical cached prefix and computes only the remaining suffix.

Task:
input.source_suffix_text: Describe the latency components that should be measured in this comparison.
input.modified_suffix_text: State the correctness checks needed before interpreting any observed speedup.

input.prefix_text:
A research team collected repeated measurements from several accelerators. Each record contains mean latency, tail latency, cache occupancy, admitted requests, rejected requests, and bytes reloaded after eviction. They want a short report that separates direct measurements from derived ratios.

Task:
input.source_suffix_text: Write a concise description of an appropriate aggregation procedure.
input.modified_suffix_text: Explain how the team should report variability and derived percentage changes.

input.prefix_text:
Consider a document-processing system that receives many requests sharing a long instruction prefix. Some suffixes are short classification questions and others request long summaries. The cache has limited capacity, so admitting every available prefix can evict entries that will be reused more often.

Task:
input.source_suffix_text: Explain why cache hit rate alone may not maximize serving utility.
input.modified_suffix_text: Give an example of a per-request admission rule based on expected benefit and cost.

input.prefix_text:
A reviewer asks whether two computational paths are equivalent. The first evaluates an entire token sequence in one forward pass. The second evaluates a shared prefix, retains the model's native key-value cache, and then evaluates the suffix with explicit attention masks and logical positions.

Task:
input.source_suffix_text: List the token-level and logit-level comparisons that address the question.
input.modified_suffix_text: Discuss why floating-point execution may prevent bitwise equality without changing decoded tokens.

input.prefix_text:
A scheduling policy estimates the time saved by reuse, subtracts lookup and transfer overhead, and penalizes expected cache pollution. The estimates are calibrated separately for each model and hardware platform because prefill cost and memory pressure differ substantially across deployments.

Task:
input.source_suffix_text: Summarize the purpose of hardware-specific calibration.
input.modified_suffix_text: Explain how the policy should behave when the estimated utility is negative.

input.prefix_text:
An experiment compares an admission controller with admit-all caching, no caching, a fixed occupancy limit, and recency-aware and frequency-aware policies. Requests arrive in several rounds, and a temporary burst creates capacity pressure before the original hot set returns. The report includes both average and tail latency.

Task:
input.source_suffix_text: Identify the measurements that reveal hot-set recovery after the burst.
input.modified_suffix_text: Describe how these baselines isolate the value of utility-aware admission.

A paper evaluates a lightweight decision layer across multiple model families and serving backends. Some integrations enforce the decision by skipping cache admission, whereas other integrations are write-through overlays that record decisions while leaving native cache behavior unchanged.

Task:
input.source_suffix_text: Explain the claim supported by the enforced experiments.
input.modified_suffix_text: Explain the narrower claim supported by the write-through compatibility experiments.
